questions.q: Profile B differs from A in D alone. One flight of A was compared with one flight of B: propwash −13 %. What can be said?
options: B is better: 13 % is more than the typical noise
Nothing: the spread within an arm is not estimated
B is better if the pilot felt the difference too
B is worse: the effect is below 15 %
questions.explain: With one flight per arm the standard deviation is undefined, and the minimum p of the permutation test is 1. In the lab the same pair showed −33 % in motor headroom, which B does not change at all.

questions.q: A session of 10 flights, and the wind picks up toward evening. Which order of A and B mixes the drift with the effect the least?
options: AAAAA BBBBB — the profiles do not get mixed up in the field
BBBBB AAAAA — the control at the end
ABBA ABBA AB — the drift is split almost evenly
Any: the number of flights is the same
questions.explain: In blocks B gets all of the late drift (in the lab +21 % against +6 % for A), and the −15 % effect disappears. In ABBA the average drift of the arms is +13.2 % and +13.8 %.

questions.q: What is the smallest two-sided p that an exact permutation test can give with 3 flights per arm?
questions.explain: The minimum p = 2 / C(2n, n). At n = 3: C(6, 3) = 20, p = 2/20 = 0.10. The 0.05 threshold is unattainable even with perfect separation; no fewer than 4 flights per arm are needed.

questions.q: Can the PID profile be switched from a switch in flight in Betaflight 4.5?
options: Yes, with function 12 in `adjrange`
Yes, with a separate PID PROFILE mode in the Modes tab
No, only the OSD and LED profiles
No: the PID profile is changed only on the ground
questions.explain: `fc/rc_adjustments.h` has no PID-profile select function, and there is no such mode either. Function 12 is RATE_PROFILE. The PID profile: the sticks while disarmed, the OSD menu, the App or `profile N`; MSP_SELECT_SETTING ignores it while armed. The gains can be written over MSP in flight, but that is not a profile change, and there is no Blackbox event.

questions.q: The slot `adjrange 0 0 3 900 2100 20 3 43 3`, and the AUX4 switch gives 988 and 2012 µs. What are the `d_roll` values?
options: 40 and 46
37 and 49
43 and 46
40 and 43
questions.explain: Absolute mode: 43 + (rc − 1500)·3/500 with C division toward zero. 988 → −3.07 → −3 → 40; 2012 → +3.07 → +3 → 46.

questions.q: In the same slot the switch gives 1100 µs in the lower position. What is the result?
options: `d_roll` = 40, as intended
`d_roll` = 41: C division dropped the fraction
The slot is not active outside the 1000–2000 µs range
`d_roll` = 39 because of rounding down
questions.explain: (1100 − 1500)·3/500 = −2.4, C integer division gives −2, and the value is 41. The channel endpoints must reach 1000 and 2000.

questions.q: The flight-to-flight spread of propwash is CV = 8 %, and the expected effect is 15 %. How many flights per arm by the course formula?
questions.explain: n ≈ 16·(CV/Δ)² = 16·(0.08/0.15)² = 4.55 → 5. In the lab at n = 5 the effect is found in 92.5 % of series, and at n = 4 — in 67 %.

questions.q: Why fly A against A once with the same program?
options: To warm up the motors before the session
To measure the metric's own noise
To check that Blackbox works on the ground
To zero the I term before B
questions.explain: An A/A test shows the spread of the metric without any effect: the CV for the plan is taken from it, and it shows the false alarm rate (about 5 % in the lab).

questions.q: Profile A is on the first 7" and profile B on a second identical one; B has 12 % less propwash. How do you get an honest conclusion?
options: Repeat the comparison on the same two drones
Swap the props and compare again
Each drone flies both profiles, the effect within the drone
Take the average of the two drones as the control
questions.explain: The aircraft and the profile change together. In the bf-pid case one profile gave a bounce-back of 2.9 and 8.5 % on two “identical” drones (the analysis there — different piloting sharpness): the “drone/session” difference is larger than the difference between profiles. A crossover design separates the profile from the aircraft.
